newsitem.title: ITALY: Buba's Gaddum - higher German tax would be unhelpful.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Gaddum - higher German tax would be unhelpful.

text.p: Bundesbank vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Saturday higher taxation in Germany at this stage in the economic cycle would not be helpful.

Gaddum, attending a conference in this lakeside Italian resort, was asked about the possibility of higher taxation by the German government in order to cover a potential shortfall in tax revenues this year.
Gaddum said the Bundesbank would not be happy with higher taxation. "Higher taxation in our cyclical situation would not be helpful. We are not friends of higher taxation."

Germany is set to release estimates of 1997 tax revenue next week and German Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said there will be a shortfall of more than 10 billion marks from estimates last November.

Analysts expect Bonn will have to act promptly to generate extra cash if it wishes to meet a three percent budget deficit to gross domestic product target required by the year end to join a single European currency in January 1999.
Gaddum said Waigel saw he could use either higher taxes or lower expenditure to cover the gap.

"If we (the Bundesbank) were to give advice we would say go to lower expenditure but the question is whether he is able to do that because of the situation in the labour market which could bring him additional expenditure and not less," he said.
On the other side of the budget equation however, he said: "Whether they have the possibility for spending cuts is really a political question."
Asked whether he thought Germany would achieve the three percent deficit to GDP target by the year end, he replied: "Our Finance Minister believes it, he says 2.9. I see the effect afterwards."
